faqLeft.q: What engine does the AMG GT 63 S use?
faqLeft.a: The AMG GT 63 S uses the M178 — a 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8. It's the same engine family as the earlier C190-generation AMG GT models, in a later, more powerful specification.

faqLeft.q: How much does an AMG GT 63 S engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £5,500. Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.

faqLeft.q: Which engine code is fitted to my AMG GT 63 S?
faqLeft.a: Enter your registration on this page and we'll confirm you have the M178 before you're quoted anything.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild M178 AMG GT 63 S engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. We replace valve cover gaskets, coolant components, bearings and gaskets as standard on every M178 rebuild.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used AMG GT 63 S engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my AMG GT 63 S if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does an AMG GT 63 S engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most AMG GT 63 S owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history, and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty — often longer and more comprehensive than what a used engine supplier offers.
